claims.claim: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science dedicated to creating systems capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence.
These tasks include things like:
Reasoning and solving complex problems.
Recognizing patterns in data, sounds, or images.
Understanding natural language (reading and speaking).
Making decisions or predictions.

Unlike traditional software, which strictly follows a rigid set of pre-written rules ("if X happens, do Y"), AI systems are designed to learn from data and adapt their behavior to new, unseen situations.
AI is generally categorized into three levels based on its capability:
Narrow AI (Weak AI):
What it is: AI designed to perform a single, specific task exceptionally well.
Status: This is the only type of AI that exists today.
Examples: Apple’s Siri, Google Maps, facial recognition, Netflix recommendations, and chess-playing computers.
Artificial General Intelligence (AGI / Strong AI):
What it is: A theoretical type of AI that possesses human-level intelligence across all domains.
It could learn, reason, plan, and adapt to any intellectual task just as a human can.
Status: Does not yet exist; it is a major goal of current research.
What it is: A hypothetical future AI that vastly surpasses the collective intellect of all humans in creativity, problem-solving, emotional intelligence, and scientific discovery.
Think of modern AI as a set of nested concepts, like Russian nesting dolls:
└── Machine Learning (ML)
└── Deep Learning (DL)
Machine Learning (ML): Instead of writing explicit code to solve a problem, engineers feed algorithms massive amounts of data.
The algorithm identifies patterns and "learns" how to make predictions or decisions on its own.
(Example: Showing an algorithm 100,000 photos of cats and dogs until it can tell them apart).
Deep Learning (DL): A specialized subset of ML based on artificial neural networks (inspired by the structure of the human brain).
It uses multiple layers of calculations to process complex data like video, audio, and written language.
Deep learning powers modern breakthroughs like self-driving cars and ChatGPT.
Generative AI: Tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Midjourney that can generate human-like text, code, images, and audio from a simple prompt.
Navigation: Google Maps or Waze predicting traffic jams and calculating the fastest route in real time.
Digital Assistants: Siri, Google Assistant, and Alexa recognizing your voice and executing commands.
Recommendation Systems: Algorithms that predict what you want to watch (Netflix/YouTube), buy (Amazon), or listen to (Spotify).
Healthcare: Algorithms that analyze X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans to detect diseases like cancer earlier and more accurately than the human eye.
Finance: Fraud-detection systems that flag suspicious credit card transactions instantly.
While AI has immense potential, it also brings significant challenges:
Bias and Fairness: If an AI is trained on biased human data, it will produce biased results (e.g., discriminatory hiring algorithms).
Job Displacement: Automation of routine cognitive and manual tasks may replace certain jobs faster than new ones are created.
Privacy: AI systems require vast amounts of personal data to train and function.
The "Black Box" Problem: Deep neural networks are often so complex that even the engineers who built them cannot explain why the AI made a specific decision.
